claims.summary: There is a universal L such that for alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 >= 1/2, X,Y independent uniform samples of size N in [0,1]^2 and any sequence t=t_N in [1,log N], with probability tending to one some matching (depending on t) has at most 2N e^(-t) pairs with |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| > L sqrt(log N/N) t^(1/alpha_j) for some j; the failure probability tends to zero uniformly in t. So each level of the ultimate matching condition common to both coordinates holds alone on and above the curve; a refutation must use mixed levels or levels coupled in one matching.
claims.assessment: Working proof: reduce to the curve by lowering 1/alpha_j; for t >= (log N)/4 thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold; below, rescale coordinate j by t^(-1/alpha_j), tile by near-square cells of about e^(2t)(log N)^2 expected points, match label-chosen equal subsamples in each cell by lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound composed through its fixed set, count leftovers and bad cells as violations, and bound their mean by 4 sqrt2 N/sqrt m + 12 N Pr(bad)^(1/2), with Markov.
claims.rationale: Shows that no argument using one level of the exponential condition common to both coordinates can refute a pair of the curve; mixed levels and the coupling of levels remain. Baseline: for exponents at most 2 thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential gives all levels at once.
claims.next_action: Build the coupling: a matching meeting all levels at once, the head item's threshold flow.

relationships: The level counts the condition implies are the ones met here, one common level at a time.
Per-level bounds do not glue into one matching in general.
At (4,4), where the cells are squares, its matchings use label-chosen leftovers, which that theorem forbids for a matching good at all levels.
For exponents at most 2 that theorem gives all levels in one matching, stronger than this one.
Each level common to both coordinates holds alone on and above the curve.
